subject: Request: standard unit pricing, IO split, and hosted model index
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@aurorahealth.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@aurorahealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing request: hosted unit rates and model roster

Hi Vanessa,

We're evaluating Redwood for a new clinical summarization and triage pipeline. Procurement asked for a concise summary: standard per-1M token unit pricing (input vs output), and a current list of hosted model families you support (and which are recommended for low-latency vs high-quality use cases).

A few specifics that would help:
- Baseline input / output rates per 1M tokens on hosted API (no discounts)
- Any published IO split guidance (how you count tokens for prompts vs responses)
- Model names / shorthand with a one-line recommended use-case (e.g., real-time assistant, long-generation summarization)
- Any quick notes on embedding costs (are they billed differently?)

We're in discovery — initial volumes likely ~2–5M tokens/month, with spikes during pilots. If you can get this over to us today or tomorrow, procurement will use it to decide whether to move the SOW to legal.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of ML Engineering
Aurora Health
attachments: Aurora_RFP_Summary_20261109.pdf

Subject: Re: Pricing request: hosted unit rates and model roster

Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask and the RFP summary. I'm attaching a compact ratecard and a pointer to our hosted model index. Quick answers up front, then a few clarifying Qs so we can recommend the optimal tier and any applicable short-term discounts: attached => redwood-hosted-ratecard-2026.xlsx, link => https://redwood.app/model-index/hosted-2026

Short answers (baseline, public hosted API rates — no enterprise commit):
- Input tokens: $0.10 per 1,000 (equivalently $100 per 1M)
- Output tokens: $0.20 per 1,000 (equivalently $200 per 1M)
- We bill tokens on the total input+output; we also surface the IO split per request in the dashboard for charge breakdowns.
- Embeddings: billed separately at $0.50 per 1,000 embedding vectors (commonly shown as $500 per 1M embedding requests; depends on vector size).

Couple of clarification Qs so Ben/Marissa and I can tailor any pricing or mention pilot discounts:
1) For the pilot, do you expect many short (few-token) requests or fewer long generations (>=1k tokens each)?
2) Any required SLA or HIPAA/data residency constraints?
3) Are you planning to use streaming responses or batch calls for the summarization jobs?

If you prefer, Ben can prepare a one-page commercial summary with a 6- and 12-month committed discount band this afternoon.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks Vanessa — helpful. Quick answers to your questions:
- Workload profile: mix, but for the pilot ~70% short prompts (100–300 tokens) and ~30% long single-shot summarizations (800–1,500 tokens output).
- Data controls: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and the ability to route processing to US regions only. HIPAA applicability is being evaluated — likely required for production.
- We'll use streaming for the UI assistants and batch for nightly summarization jobs.

Please do send a 1-page commercial with mid-term (6/12 month) discount bands — procurement will want ranges. Also clarify whether your published IO split billing example counts everything as combined (i.e., we pay based on total tokens) or if you ever bill input/output separately on invoices for transparency.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alex
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Alex —

Appreciate the context. Attached is a concise commercial summary and a baseline rate table; below is the exact text you can paste into procurement if helpful.

--- BEGIN PRICING BLURB FOR PROCUREMENT ---
Redwood Hosted API (public, list prices, no commit):
- Input tokens: $100 per 1,000,000 tokens (billed at $0.0001 per token)
- Output tokens: $200 per 1,000,000 tokens (billed at $0.0002 per token)
- Billing model: invoices show combined total and a token-level IO breakdown; legally we charge for total tokens, but line-item split is provided for transparency.
- Embeddings: $500 per 1,000,000 embedding calls (billing depends on vector size; confirm vector dimension for precise quoting).

Model guidance (hosted index snapshot):
- swift-7b (low-latency assistant): best for UI assistants with streaming; lower cost, faster response times.
- atlas-13b (balanced quality/latency): recommended for most summarization and triage workloads.
- titan-xl (high-quality, long-context): recommended for single-shot long generative summaries and extraction tasks.

Discount bands (indicative, subject to contract and volume verification):
- 6-month commit (>=50k USD/month): 10–18% off published IO rates
- 12-month commit (>=40k USD/month): 18–28% off published IO rates + standard enterprise support SLA

Compliance & Residency: SOC 2 Type II report is available upon NDA. US-region processing and VPC/private deployments supported for production (we can scope HIPAA controls in Private offering).
--- END PRICING BLURB ---

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben will draft the 1-page commercial with two commit scenarios and include an example pro-forma invoice showing IO split (will attach).
2) If procurement likes the numbers, we can follow with an NDA/SOC2 exchange and a quick tech call on regional processing options.

Ben / Marissa: can one of you send the 1-pager + pro-forma before COB PST?

Thanks — talk soon.
